label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.
read: RC2 30-page edition, draft PDF, 32 pages, built from dev at 5bde59a3 with the publisher's command (a local copy of the figures list for chapter 1's new Figure line)
first_impression: The cover and the little characters made me want to flip on, but inside there are ten dashed 'Figure to come' boxes where pictures should be and several nearly empty pages.

pages.what_i_see: Dark cover with six colour-coded character cards and a rainbow corner. Friendly, lets a non-programmer see 'people', not code. Only six of the nine shown, which the title does not explain.
Title page: big title, author, subtitle, then a lot of white. Plenty of air, near-empty but acceptable for a title page.
Contents page: six chapter names in a plain list in the top-left, no page numbers, the rest of the page blank. Reads as a mistake, not a design.

Chapter 1 opens well: cast bar, small narrator head, then a two-half infographic with speech bubbles and an A-to-B arrow. Clear and funny. At the foot a dashed 'Figure to come: the player as I saw it' box is printed as text and splits across the page break, so the picture the words describe is missing.

The tail of the dashed 'Figure to come' box sits orphaned at the top (a file path in small type), then body text. The player screenshot the editor wants is not there. Rest of the page breathes well; the 'Words' idea is not used here.

Loop infographic (circle of three arrows, tiny factory inside) at the top works as the second half of the slide-versus-loop picture, but it is separated from its first half on page 4 by a full page. Quote and body text breathe.

'Words on this page' box is helpful (agent, player). The row of ten greyed cast cards is clipped at the right edge (fifth card cut off) and the caption under it is a long dense line. Page is full: a 'Where this came from' paragraph starts at the foot and runs over.
Five lines of source note carried over from page 7, then blank. A widow page: nearly empty.
Good page: dramatised scene with Dev and Conductor, one head per speaker run, moods in italics, two glossary boxes. Slightly dense but readable.

Four lit cast cards with arrival times are a nice summary, but the greyed row of five beneath is clipped at the right edge and its labels (researcher, storyteller) squeeze against the card edges. Page is crowded: scene, cards, caption and note all stacked.

A dashed 'Figure to come: the factory as a chain' box where the Wardley map should be, and the text then says 'Look at the bottom row first'. Missing picture, and the key one for understanding the factory. The glossary box (wardley map, wake) is good.

Strong picture: the clock dial with each agent at its minute and the five-step loop in the middle. The legend is two columns and a little cramped, but this one helps. The next section heading sits at the foot with only a few lines under it: tight.
Reviewer exchange then the card of the first five-step wake with a big '162'. The record card helps. The small cast-bar strip near the foot is a pleasant touch. Heavy but breathes.
Short 'Do this now' and 'Where this came from', then about two thirds blank. The 'Do this now' italic line sits tight against the narrator line above it.
Bar chart of wakes by hour is clear and shows the empty chair gap well. Good page. The cast bar text is a bit long.
Two-panel reviewer/researcher card sits close under the text but works. The scene runs on the next page; heading 'Sent back, and owned' near the foot with four lines under it is acceptable.
Three 'sent back' cards in a row help. Page is dense: text, many speaker heads and the cards with little air between them. A shorter run of heads would help.
Afternoon timeline picture is good. Then a dashed 'Figure to come: the map of the day' box, where the words describe who was on stage when. Missing picture.
Diagram of the relayed word stopped at studio's door, with a straight question to the editor, is clear and funny. Good page, breathes.
Short 'Do this now' and a source note, then most of the page blank.
Dot timeline of the last ten minutes helps, labels a little small. Glossary box (lock, freeze) is useful. Page is crowded: picture, caption, box and a three-speaker scene.
Hold diagram (wake clock with HOLD file) beside the big '82 seconds' card works well. A heading at the foot ('Why stop then') with two lines under it: slightly tight.

A dashed 'Figure to come: three speech cards' box where the three reasons should be shown. The interview strip below has six cards squeezed edge to edge and the last is clipped at the right edge: too tight.
Row of 'did not work' cards is a good summary and honest. Page text is dense. The speaker-and-mood lines (Deck, Storyteller) are easy to follow.
Empty-chair strip is funny and clear but the last card is clipped at the right edge. The 'Do this now' and 'Where this came from' run to the foot, the source note spilling onto the next page.
Four lines of source note, then blank: widow page.

Chapter 4 opens with a dashed 'Figure to come: the nine cast cards turning into files' box. Missing. The list of the second factory's team in the cast is a good idea but entries use plain small heads.
A dashed 'Figure to come: this book's team as cast cards' box sits in the middle of a very dense page of dialogue and narration. Missing picture, and the page is too tight.
Two dashed boxes on one page ('two cards from this book's record' and 'three people, each with a small factory'). Both missing pictures; the page reads as plans with no drawings.

The practical page. A dashed 'Map to come' box at the top where the map is meant. The five numbered step cards are the best part: a step I could take tomorrow, with 'What to do' and 'What to check'. Slightly dense.
Another dashed 'Figure to come: the five steps as a path' box, where the steps picture should be, then a 'Do this now', and a source note. Reasonable air.
Back page about the series, short and warm, then blank. Fine as a closing page.

pictures_that_work: 1: the six cast cards on the cover; I can see who is who
4: the slide-versus-loop picture with speech bubbles; it shows the problem in one glance
12: the clock dial with the five-step loop; the best picture in the book
13: the first-wake card with the 162 figure
15: the wakes-by-hour bar chart showing the empty chair
19: the relayed word stopped at studio's door
22: the HOLD file card beside the 82 seconds figure
24: the 'did not work' cards, honest and easy to scan
30: the five numbered steps with what to do and what to check
pictures_missing: 4-5: the talk's player UI the chapter describes (slide, countdown, step controls, notes); only a dashed text box, split across the page break
11: the Wardley map ('Look at the bottom row first') is a dashed box
18: the map of the day, who was on stage when
23: the three speech cards giving three reasons for stopping
27: the nine cast cards turning into files
28: this book's team as cast cards
29: two cards from this book's own record (refusal, usage limit)
29: three people each with a small factory joined by a brief, board and hold
30: the map of parts for my own factory
31: the five steps as a path
too_tight: 7: ten greyed cast cards clipped at the right edge; dense caption
10: greyed card row clipped at the right and labels squeezed; cards, caption and note stacked
12: heading at the foot with only a few lines under it; cramped legend
14: 'Do this now' italic line jammed against the narrator line
17: many speaker heads and three cards with little air
21: picture, caption, glossary box and a three-speaker scene all on one page
23: interview strip of six cards edge to edge, last one clipped
25: empty-chair strip last card clipped at the right edge
28: a very dense page of dialogue with a missing figure inside it
Near-empty pages: 3 (contents list only), 8, 14, 20, 26 (source notes carried over, then blank)
speakers_note: Colour-coded heads and italic moods make the speakers easy to follow, and runs of Dev, Conductor and Deck mostly sit under one head with the mood shown (page 9). The Narrator head is still repeated on many consecutive paragraphs, for example pages 16, 17 and 28, which makes pages look busier than they are.
words_on_this_page_boxes: They help me most, as a newcomer: pages 7, 9, 11, 21 and 27 explain agent, repository, commit, hold, wake, lock and session in plain words just when I meet them. The tone of the scenes ('I would staff it first, next time') is cheeky and warm. More of them in chapter 2 and 3 where I met 'pre-review' and 'register' without a box.
top_three_fixes: Replace the ten dashed 'Figure to come' boxes with real pictures, starting with the player UI on pages 4-5 and the Wardley map on page 11.
Fix the cards clipped at the right edge (pages 7, 10, 23, 25) and give pages 17, 21 and 28 more air.
Put the contents page numbers in, and stop source notes landing alone on near-empty pages (8, 14, 20, 26).
notes: The practical page 30 is what I would act on tomorrow: tool, rules, brief, ship small, add a second agent. The words 'wake', 'register' and 'pre-review' still lost me a little, but the boxes catch most of them. Page 3 contents without numbers looks unfinished.
